This is a dated implementation record for framework contributors. Each entry records the APIs, tests, failures, and open work at that point; words such as "current", "now", and "remaining" refer to the entry's date. Older entries can therefore describe gaps that later entries close. Test counts, timings, hashes, and compatibility scopes are retained as evidence, not current guarantees.

The 2026-09-20 framework completion scope defers exhaustive parity across every game. Use the release assessment and support envelope for that decision and its limits; use getting started for the current authoring path. The original roadmap, separate ports, and comparisons remain references. Keep original projects and their Replay ports independently runnable. Add only observed evidence to this log.

Framework-first closure assessment — 2026-09-20#

The revised framework-first queue is complete. The support assessment maps modes, transports, platforms, resource limits and authoring/runtime tradeoffs, and retains Replay as experimental alongside Kit. A real native service-kill case clears Party readiness after 10.46 seconds while admitted encrypted links reach the tick-1200 reference. Automatic background control reconnect is explicitly unsupported.

The actual Nix addon recipe builds from a frozen current snapshot and runs in an external consumer project using only packaged collection/build inputs. Offline, host/client/observer and actual Chrome export cases pass; all 233 packaged Replay source files match the snapshot. No artifact was published. The latest framework smoke already covers 400 unit tests plus recipes/target/archive checks.

See the final audit, support envelope and final receipts. Original frameworks/projects remain preserved. Deferred full-game parity and broader live Steam/platform/public-deployment work are not represented as finished.

Endpoint separation and framework onboarding — 2026-09-20#

P2P_Direct_Options.listen now selects a local address/port independently of the advertised endpoint. Defaults preserve existing behavior; malformed values fail before opening the listener. Fifteen adapter tests/WASM checks pass. A real native TLS/ENet case advertises UDP forwarding ports while binding distinct local ports, then repeats that separation for a returning creator. Encrypted gameplay converges at tick 600 and the survivor follows the new advertised endpoint.

The framework now has a consolidated getting-started guide, compatibility policy, native/WASM checked lifecycle recipes and a bounded smoke command with individual receipts. No new game-content matrix was added. See delivery evidence. The remaining shared task is the supported-envelope/release assessment, including explicit classification of failed P2P control reconnection.

Shared framework acceptance audit — 2026-09-20#

The eight completion gates now map to current APIs, test coverage and explicit support boundaries. Selected suites pass 362 unit tests plus target/recording checks. One current four-process observer fault/refresh capture delivers all 21 kicks, preserves the pending confirmed effect exactly once and replays identically on native/WASM through tick 2400. The old unrecorded C2 failure remains historically unexplained; it does not justify another open-ended game parity campaign.

The audit exposed an optimized native P2P corpus crash. IR/assembly and debugger evidence show a compiler register-clobber miscompile of an inlined test-model factory. A fixture-only no-inline boundary preserves direct model calls; the full default/optimized native/WASM P2P command now passes. No runner behavior was changed. Stale README/architecture/recovery capability claims and the old checkpoint protocol-number description were corrected.

The audit leaves three concrete areas in the closure queue: native bind/advertised endpoint separation, setup/recovery/compatibility documentation and a supported-envelope release assessment. Original projects remain preserved. Focused receipts retain the failure and final checks without duplicating the codebase.

Native P2P admission integration — 2026-09-20#

P2P_Direct now owns two-player authenticated ENet, endpoint discovery and physical connection replacement over the reusable Party/pair-key APIs. Registration and pair replies share separate Router lanes on one control socket. Each process registers its current endpoint without rewriting its immutable enrollment request.

Real native TLS cases pass for creator and guest return after process kill. Both advance incarnation, retain the survivor's runner and converge at tick 600 to 9353382615414616636. Creator return changes ports and the survivor follows the new signed endpoint. A browser rejoin regression still reaches its tick-900 reference. Seven link, sixteen provisioning and fourteen adapter tests/WASM pass. The exposed double-disconnect cleanup error is fixed; signed registration refusal also clears native link keys.

This closes the focused two-player native admission integration. Public deployment, independent crypto review, other topologies/platforms and the remaining shared framework audit stay explicit. See receipts and the finite closure queue. Original projects are preserved.

Priority correction — framework first, 2026-09-20#

Full game-by-game parity is no longer the framework completion gate. Ports serve as representative integration tests and authoring examples. The current work is native P2P admission; next comes a finite audit of shared APIs/correctness gaps, then stabilization and delivery. Game-only content/presentation differences move to follow-up. No deferred item is being represented as verified parity.

Native admission foundation now has a per-pair authenticated/encrypted transport and an optional registered-member pair-key service. Seven link tests and sixteen P2P provisioning tests pass, including WASM checks. These are core tests, not native gameplay acceptance. The next step is to connect the pair service/client and link wrapper to the native party/ENet owner. See link contract and pair service. Current receipts are in /private/tmp/replay-native-link-20260920/{link-first,pairs-tests}.log; no game parity campaign was added for this framework-only increment.

M7 P2P party client and browser Duel integration — 2026-09-20#

The reusable registration client now performs challenged process rebind, waits for a complete roster and maintains authenticated roster reads. Godot P2P_Party composes it with the existing durable enrollment/profile owner. A separate Duel service combines bounded private SQLite rooms and authenticated mesh signaling. Browser Duel now creates, joins and rejoins through this service, deriving runner scope from the enrolled match rather than test session 123.

Thirteen core/client/provider tests, thirteen Godot adapter tests, WASM checking and the native ENet Duel regression pass. Two final independent-profile Chrome cases exercise the real invitation controls, forced guest-before-creator signaling, packet faults, a participant download, process kill and durable rejoin. Both guest and creator returns advance incarnation 2 to 3, preserve the surviving runner and converge at tick 900 to hash 826411474463535637. Creator return also retains RTC ID 1 while advancing the connection generation. The sharing UI now provides a DOM Copy button and selectable fallback after Godot's queued callback exposed a Web clipboard limitation. A real permission-denial/success pair verifies that flow.

The native launcher keeps its existing ENet mode; provisioned native gameplay admission, public TLS/TURN deployment, broader outages, accounts and human review remain work. Original projects and sibling Scrapyard are preserved. See client contract and evidence/limits. M0–M9 remains active.

M7 durable fixed-roster P2P provisioning — 2026-09-20#

replay/p2p/provision now owns a durable 2–8 player enrollment count, bounded room service, seat-reserving invitations, exact enrollment retries and authenticated roster/registration operations. It reuses the existing enrollment protocol and client journal. No member receives simulation authority, and authority commands and removal extensions are unreachable through the P2P control entry point.

The native SQLite backend persists count, credentials, invites and request frontiers in one revision. The Godot signaling provider reads committed membership for every admission, so rebind invalidates old incarnations without changing the match code. Ten core/client/provider tests, WASM checking, three SQLite tests and process kills before/after commit pass. A separate native Godot TLS server/client fixture creates three enrollments and reopens them in fresh processes with identical keys and a newer incarnation. Existing authority/provisioning/admission suites also pass.

This is the provisioning foundation, not a completed public P2P game flow. Duel's client owner/menu, browser enrollment and signaling/gameplay integration remain next; human accounts and public deployment also remain open. Originals are preserved and the full M0–M9 goal remains active. See contract and evidence.

M3/M5 native Steam Room lifecycle integration — 2026-09-20#

Room now accepts the native Steam gameplay backend through explicit canonical Steam-ID/virtual-port endpoints and fresh peer construction. Registration binds the local initialized runtime ID; signed coordinator grants determine remote targets. Bootstrap, redirect, takeover, old-host return and published restore share target validation before destructive connection changes. Existing endpoint/RPC/save schemas remain unchanged.

Four endpoint/core tests, the existing Steam adapter/Session contract suite and new factory/endpoint failure cases pass. Four carrier recovery cases, repeated handoff to epoch three and fresh-process return pass through Steam-shaped API objects backed by local ENet, with exact host/client call destinations, fresh peers and virtual ports zero/65535. Native ENet and Chrome RTC recovery/save regressions also pass. These are not Valve network packets or live-account acceptance.

No app ID, live host/test role or addon was configured; an isolated live test setup has been requested. Live multi-account Steam, lobby UX, SteamGameServer and broader platform/deployment gates remain open. See contract and evidence/limits. Originals remain preserved and the full M0–M9 goal stays active.

M2 shared runtime aliases accepted without losing tag guardrails — 2026-09-20#

Scriptgen now proves an unresolved shared type has no inline Godot metadata before accepting it. The proof follows aliases and generics in their defining/caller import contexts, recognizes engine/stdlib leaves and stays bounded. Tagged fields, methods, ticks and signals remain refused, including aliases and ambiguous gd imports. Hello now declares its actual field as game.Timeline.

Thirty-one focused cases and the existing full generator suite pass. Isolated Kit Cavecrawl/Quickdraw/Speedball generated outputs are byte-identical to the previous generator. Native/WASM Hello, four-rate input and same-frame pause tests, delayed networking, rendered/native/Chrome editing, export/import, playback and branching pass. The failed stdlib and engine-alias collision candidates remain recorded.

The M2 ledger closes this concrete authoring defect while retaining human visual/play-feel review. Original sources and pre-existing unrelated generator changes are preserved. See implementation/evidence. The complete M0–M9 goal remains active.

M2 acceptance audit and ordinary Hello pause fix — 2026-09-20#

An actual Godot baseline reproduced a paused fire tap leaking into resumed play. Hello now discards paused gameplay edges/clock remainder and gates already-held controls until release. Native 30/60/120/144-FPS and real Chrome keyboard cases pass; explicit production-process timing gives identical 60-tick/five-shot/160-unit movement per second, preserves short presses and bounds catch-up. The complete native/rendered/Chrome history, field editing, export/import, playback, branching and delayed network regressions pass. Core/view/diagnostic suites total 64 tests, with native/WASM recording execution.

The M2 audit now lists concrete evidence for every implementation item and acceptance gate. It also reproduces the still-open shared Timeline alias scriptgen failure and retains the human visual/play-feel review requirement. M2 is not marked complete. See baseline failure and current receipts. Originals remain preserved, and full M0–M9 work remains active.

M4/M5 durable host moderation and successor exclusion — 2026-09-20#

Cavecrawl now has a host-only named player selector and removal control. Direct sessions retain checkpointed token bans; Room queues a separate authenticated coordinator operation and reports its durable result. Disabling a member atomically invalidates its prepared nomination and records the request frontier. Room mirrors the disabled roster before gameplay/restore and selects another eligible successor.

Thirty-six authority, twelve provisioning and 182 network tests pass, along with frozen old/new RPC compatibility and SQLite kills before/after commit. Native removal of a prepared member two, fresh-process denial, replacement by member three, planned/crash takeover and continued loot pass. Unsupported-service and all-removal- replies-lost cases preserve lease progress and resolve boundedly. Chrome planned/ crash cases verify actual RTC traffic and continued play. Rendered native selector rename/removal, the full C9 campaign and all owner-profile carrier regressions pass.

Revoked credentials authenticate only a minimal denial. The game block is scoped to the room identity; invitations and independently authorized new identities remain separate. Game content/save schemas and original projects are preserved. See contract, Room integration and evidence/failed fixtures. Broader UX/deployment, other game integrations and full M0–M9 acceptance remain open.

M2/M4 bounded rock motion between simulation ticks — 2026-09-20#

view.Tick_Phase and Godot's session_tick_phase now track bounded render progress against actual simulation heads. Stalls cannot wrap visuals backward; fencing and pause hold them, and view/epoch changes reset scope. Observer phase starts at snapshot arrival. Cavecrawl previews each live rock by at most one tick, clips against visible bodies without applying hits, and centers its authored glyph. C9/O3 simulation/content/save contracts remain unchanged.

Six final native cases cover both motion profiles at 30/60/144 FPS with separate host/client/observer processes and 120 ms receive delay. Every sampled same-tick pair moves forward, with one-tick bounds, no backward step on advancing heads and no expired views. The initial 144-FPS observer cohort failed the stronger continuity gate; its unrelated local-clock seed is fixed and the rejected evidence is retained.

Twenty-four view tests/WASM, four model/adapter tests, both native visual contracts, rendered/Chrome checks and all three normal/owner/faulted full campaigns pass. Complete frame hashes remain unchanged by visual sampling. Pre-tick cast/contact prediction, broader parity, deployment and the full roadmap remain open. See API, game behavior and evidence.

M4 generation-bound dweller impacts and C9/O3 compatibility — 2026-09-20#

Rock contacts now emit a copied-pose dweller Hit, with projectile occurrence identity and exact target generation/slot. Yellow sparks and red flashes survive source removal without tinting a recycled body. Damage/collision behavior and saved world layout stay unchanged; the new event sequence is explicitly versioned as C9/O3. Genuine C8/O2 saves convert with exact frame and ledger preservation. Their recordings retain explicit historical models; native/WASM verification rejects the new event rules when deliberately substituted. All 18 C1–C8/O1–O2 save fixtures convert safely.

C9 normal/faulted and final O3 campaigns present 24 dweller impacts on all peers, retaining complete gameplay/hash checks. Native generation/color/cancellation, rendered and Chrome lifecycle checks pass, as do both current typed checkpoint backends and Chrome O3 planned/crash/save gates. The 35 base, 12 owner and two compatibility tests pass, with actual WASM archive continuation/verification.

An O3 campaign failure exposed a hard-coded heal expectation after live enemy damage. A diagnostic recorded 30→20 from a bite, then a correct 20→45 heal. The revised fixture verifies exact authoritative healing, stamina, cooldown and action acceptance; the failed runs remain recorded. See evidence and limits. Originals remain preserved; remaining parity, deployment and full-roadmap gates stay open.

M2/M4 bounded visual cues and Cavecrawl combat feedback — 2026-09-20#

view.Cues(Value) now maps journal changes into a bounded pool of detached visual instances. Unique renderer keys, retained consumed IDs, explicit epoch reset, correction, confirmation, cancellation and expiry share one typed helper. Copied values reject reference-bearing payloads. Full pools drop cosmetic work explicitly.

Cavecrawl's common frontend now renders player/dweller death bursts and player hit sparks/flashes, using the original particle settings/colors. The ordinary and faulted server-motion campaigns and owner-motion campaign each present two player deaths, twelve slain dwellers and five player hits on all three processes, alongside the unchanged full campaign/world-hash gates. Native/rendered lifecycle checks, actual color checks, 22 view tests/WASM and Chrome particle lifecycle checks pass.

The simulation, content and save schemas remain unchanged. Nonlethal dweller Hit occurrences, render-rate rock presentation and broader visual parity remain open; bite feedback is broader than the original rock-tracer contact renderer. The parity ledger also now explicitly tracks missing moderation UI and coordinated revocation, and reflects the already completed owner/browser/comparison work. See cue API, game behavior and receipts. Full M0–M9 completion remains open.

M3/M9 compact recent-fact bundles — 2026-09-20#

The recent-fact redundancy stream now optionally shares its envelope and connection scope across up to four facts. Feature 4096/kind 27 retains complete occurrences, recipient filtering, independent packet decoding and the same reliable stream, four-tick window and send cadence. Four empty entries cost 81 instead of 389 bytes. Older peers keep the previous encoding; Session exposes an opt-out.

The separate Replay Speedball now has a pure complete-pitch model, reusable momentum/rolling/contact helpers, predicted kicks/spikes/goals, authoritative score presentation and correction smoothing. The original game and scenes remain unchanged; copied scene provenance and the intent-only spike validation difference are documented. The runner's existing one-action-per-seat-per-tick policy services the two-command burst on successive ticks. This is an initial port, not full UI/platform/parity completion.

The four-process ENet receipt passes at 240 ms RTT: two spikes accepted once, actual Godot-node displacement over 12 game pixels in three ticks / 44 ms before acknowledgement, predicted local kicks, one canceled/replaced remote speculative flash, exactly two observer kick effects, and matching 0–1 score/winner/centered ball. Maximum recorded ball correction was 268.602 game pixels, including possible reset disagreements; visual quality and detailed cause/CPU measurements remain open. This is not a paired Kit comparison.

This port exposed stale remote guesses during state correction. A native regression failed with −2 versus the expected −14 remote position. The runner now seeds remote prediction from the latest authoritative held-input boundary and applies hold once per replayed/live prediction tick. Local controls, action IDs and aiming stamps remain exact. Core correction can atomically rewrite guessed suffix inputs; late replay failure preserves the previous inputs/state/events. Detached correction notices compare one prediction tick before/after replay, letting views smooth correction independently from forward movement. A large-world WASM fixture now keeps its runtime owner on the heap instead of exceeding the stack warning limit.

Validation: 15 core tests/headless loot, 36 network tests, 12 view tests, five Speedball model tests, 24 authority tests and nine recovery tests, with their WASM fixtures. Speedball solo/network gates and Quickdraw's normal and planned/crash combat migration gates passed after the replay change. One Odin build exited with signal 11; later builds passed, without an established compiler fix. The complete legacy suite was not rerun. Claimball/partial prediction, broader game parity, M4 owner streams and M7–M9 remain active work.

M5/M6 live Quickdraw combat recovery — 2026-09-05#

Quickdraw now uses the same Room driver as Cavecrawl for explicit trusted-member hosting and takeover. Its four-process gate requests handoff or kills the host after combat has produced a dead target awaiting respawn, flying lobs, active weapon cooldowns, equipment and collision history. The new authority reads its installed baseline and compares the entire frame with the exact approved archive; the test then requires new hits, respawn, a new purchase and matching canonical world digests at a common tick on all surviving clients. Planned mode also checks that the old host rejoins seat 1. Both modes pass at 240 ms gameplay RTT.

Session_Options.remote_observed preserves local/remote effect policy through role changes. Quickdraw resets views on epoch/Welcome changes and scopes beam cancellation to the full occurrence ID. Recovery now reports installation wall time, and takeover reuses the existing receiver's schema cache before releasing the old Session. A native authority test verifies the restored runtime remains valid after that cache is destroyed.

Latest recorded combat migration receipts: planned checkpoint 127, no known lost ticks, 1,415 ms trigger-to-ready for the surviving shooter; crash checkpoint 131, 28 known lost ticks, 2,508 ms trigger-to-ready. Installed archives were 6,262 / 6,226 bytes; measured runtime installation took 47,434 / 37,848 microseconds. These are single-run wall-time receipts, not CPU percentiles or an old/new-framework performance comparison. Some initial shots after rejoin had no valid observed bracket and correctly missed; later historical queries and gameplay continued.

Validation: Quickdraw planned/crash migration, normal duel/lob gate (15 historical hits vs zero live, all effects, 13 predicted/landed lobs at a 16 ms maximum local sample-to-node delay), five native Quickdraw tests/WASM, 24 authority tests/WASM, and the existing Cavecrawl planned migration gate. The complete legacy suite was not rerun. M6 still needs ball-game ports, prediction scopes and broader parity; M4 owner streams and M7–M9 remain open.

Two existing scriptgen interop limits surfaced while adding the harness: a direct untagged game.Controls field from res://shared was rejected as an unresolved bundle, and a method parameter declared as Odin string received a Godot String constructor without conversion. The harness now stores scalar device input and uses an explicitly owned gd.String parameter/conversion. Original scriptgen and Kit sources are unchanged. Fixing those authoring paths with generator regression tests remains an M2/M9 ergonomics item; the workaround is not a general solution.

M6 initial Quickdraw slice — 2026-09-05#

The separate Replay Quickdraw project now ports movement/dash, hitscan, HP/death/respawn, gold/boots, independent drone steering and predicted lobs into a complete Odin world. Original Quickdraw and sibling Scrapyard remain unchanged. Arena/view asset provenance is recorded.

The runner adds Model.step_view, input-bound observed snapshot brackets, bounded authority-side query validation and Model.event_owner with an opt-in mixed presentation policy. replay/history stores copied collision proxies inside the world; ray queries never temporarily reposition live entities. Rejected/expired view contexts disable historical queries while valid movement continues. Complete archives retain validated view contexts and collision history. Gameplay protocol is now 6 and archive format 4; older experimental formats reject explicitly.

The recorded three-process ENet gate passed at 240 ms injected RTT: 15 historical hits versus zero live hits, 20/20 local and watched effects in both shot phases, and 13 predicted lobs subsequently confirmed as landed on all processes. Each predicted projectile's Godot node appeared before authority acknowledgement; maximum sample-to-node delay was 16 ms. Two purchases settled once in the lob phase. The record includes raw logs, application bytes, correction/replay counts and a prior unexplained development-run effect discrepancy that remains a fault/performance coverage item.

Validation for this increment: five native Quickdraw scenarios plus WASM type-check, 33 network scenarios plus WASM, 14 core tests/headless loot, 12 view tests, 24 authority tests and nine recovery tests with their WASM fixtures. Real Godot solo Quickdraw, Cavecrawl process-crash save/resume and coordinated planned migration passed after the protocol change. The latter reached epoch 2 with zero known lost ticks and a 580 ms reported interruption. The complete legacy suite was not rerun.

At that initial slice, remaining M6 work included Quickdraw UI/scenario/fault parity, detailed correction/CPU metrics, live competitive migration (now covered by the increment above), Speedball/Claimball and authored prediction scope/boundary handling remain. Full-world prediction with mixed presentation is not partial prediction. M4 owner streams/parity and M7–M9 also remain open.

Completed increments#

  • M0: architecture, implementation sequence, source baseline inventory, and paired-game comparison protocol written.
  • M1: typed complete-world history, input revision, atomic suffix replay, pools/RNG/lifetime, local audit, and checkpoint continuation. Eleven native tests plus the headless loot example and WASM type-check passed.
  • M2 initial implementation: bounded event journal with Begin/Update/Cancel/ Confirm, speculative/confirmed/watched policies, monotonic confirmation, queue backpressure, frame/pose sampling, positional smoothing, fixed-step clock, buffered button edges, static 2D kinematics/cooldowns, and a Godot Node2D map. Separate Hello and Loot scenes compile and pass real headless Godot tests. Scene resource ownership is explicitly retained/released; the gates reject leaked-resource engine errors.
  • M3 foundations: canonical field codecs with public/authority projections, versioned/checksummed envelopes, whole-world authoritative correction and explicit resync, deterministic fault transport, and a direct Godot ENet adapter. The adapter transferred and validated world envelopes over both delivery modes in a server plus two-client test, including a fresh project-cache startup.
  • M3 gameplay runner: typed server/client/observer model, seat/connection admission, token digests, tick-stamped controls, reliable sequenced actions and verdicts, authoritative facts/snapshots, prediction/correction, explicit blackout resync, reconnect, observed frame history, and input-lead adjustment. The Hello network scene passes a four-process ENet gameplay gate at 120 ms receive delay on each process.
  • M3 snapshot protocol: acknowledged canonical baselines, sparse XOR deltas, bounded sender/receiver caches, missing-baseline full recovery, compact facts, rotating outbound scheduling, and per-peer/per-pump egress budgets. Protocol version 2 passes native and real Godot gameplay gates. A paired Hello-model trace produces identical simulation state with compression on/off and more than 50% lower application traffic in that scenario. This is a protocol comparison, not the later old-framework-versus-Replay game comparison.

Current focused validation includes 14 core tests, 11 presentation/game tests, 9 schema tests, 5 deterministic transport tests, WASM type-checks, the headless loot executable, both Godot scene acceptance tests, and the three-process ENet transport/codec gate. The runner now has twenty-four engine-free scenarios plus four standalone delta/cache tests, a WASM type-check, and four-process real gameplay acceptance. Individual gates are rerun when their dependencies change. The complete legacy repository suite has not been rerun for this additive increment.

Latest verified Godot receipts:

Text
REPLAY_HELLO_WALK x=144.000015258789
REPLAY_HELLO_RESTORE tick=2 views=3
REPLAY_HELLO_OK
REPLAY_LOOT_VIEW_OK

Remaining M2 follow-through#

  • Expanded frame-sampling/confirmation tests and the WASM fixture pass; keep them green.
  • Human visual/play-feel review has not been performed. The tests establish view lifetime/input/effect behavior, not subjective polish.
  • More specialized physics, angular correction smoothing, animation/audio effect adapters, and new codegen sugar should follow concrete game requirements.
  • Existing scriptgen accepts direct generic replay.Timeline(...) fields, but rejects a shared-package alias to that runtime as an unresolved tagged bundle. The examples spell the generic directly. Revisit alias diagnostics during authoring stabilization rather than silently weakening Kit's existing checks.

Next milestone#

M4 is underway: basic room controls and a separate Cavecrawl implementation now exist. Locks, custom admission, kicks, bans/unbans, and explicit seat replacement are implemented; fresh-occupant initialization is a tick input. Twenty-four runner tests pass, including lock/reconnect, ban, fresh-seat behavior, and checkpoints. Follow runner documentation for the implemented contract. The separate Cavecrawl model implements loot, doors, carrying, rocks, statuses, death/revive, dweller AI, waves, and floor progression. Seven pure/network-model tests plus solo and co-op Godot loot/door gates pass. Its original floor scenes and entity visuals are preserved in a separate project, with original script attachments removed. See the port's parity matrix for gaps; full original-game parity is not claimed. Automatic host migration, integrated replication/authority fencing, owner-streamed physics, and performance comparison remain open. Durable authority archives and save/resume now exist; see the latest increment below. The full roadmap goal remains active.

Tooling follow-up: immediate fresh-project --import shutdown crashed in the existing editor integration. Normal headless editor startup with 120 frames to drain queued work passed on a fresh cache; the ENet gate uses that path. Do not claim the immediate-import issue is fixed. Existing framework/game sources were not changed to work around it.

Compiler integration notes: this Odin toolchain produced nil type IDs for generic type expressions in a []typeid literal, and nil callbacks when passing the generic network thunk directly as a procedure value. Packet schemas now initialize their generic types directly, and the core receives a concrete typed thunk. Both are exercised by the instantiated runner tests; avoid reintroducing those forms.

An additional real-process run passed with REPLAY_JITTER=20, REPLAY_LOSS=1000, and REPLAY_DUPLICATE=1000, alongside 120 ms receive delay on each process. Loss/duplication affect the unreliable application channel; reliable packets retain ordering/delivery guarantees. This is not an ENet congestion/retransmission benchmark. Native tests also cover lost ACKs, missing bases, forged ACKs, outbound-rate recovery, and reliable blackouts.

The new Godot Session facade owns shared setup/pump/action/view-event routing; Cavecrawl exercises it. Input binding helpers release their retained event resources, and large snapshots use reliable fallback above the configured datagram limit. Original Kit and original Cavecrawl/Scrapyard gameplay sources remain unchanged.

Durable saves and recovery increment#

Archive v1 stores the complete authority frame (including private fields), exact network settings, roster/token hashes, room lock/bans/custom policy data, pending membership and actions/inputs, and received/settled action frontiers with recent outcomes. Decode preflights the bounded canonical body and validates the full archive before installation. A fresh authority can restore it at a newer epoch, including promotion of an existing guest seat. Pending actions are preserved or explicitly retired according to caller policy. There is no external-effect outbox.

Seven new runner scenarios bring the native suite to 24 tests, with allocator tracking and WASM instantiation of capture/codec/restore. They also exposed and fixed a same-tick rejoin/leave ordering issue and protect the host's local token against being reused for a second remote seat.

The Godot facade now supplies persistent profiles, staged archive writes/reads, session_save, and explicit session_resume. Cavecrawl provides F5 save and an opt-in resume launch. Profiles/saves are isolated from the original game. Two new real-process gates passed and are registered in the main test list:

Text
REPLAY_CAVE_SAVE_RESUME_OK tick=82 epoch=2
REPLAY_CAVE_RECOVERY_OK

The solo gate saves during an active projectile, creates an incomplete next staging file, kills the writer, checks the exact restored frame hash in a new process, and continues playing. The co-op gate restores a killed host and a restarted guest at 120 ms receive delay per process; the guest retains their reserved seat and loot, and continued actions converge. This gate supplies the new epoch explicitly and does not claim migration of a surviving client. Native macOS process recovery is verified; power-loss and browser persistence are not.

The final checks also passed the cave's seven pure gameplay tests, the complete generated cave scripts' WASM type-check (including Session/storage), the original new-port solo walk/loot/door gate, and Hello's four-process network gate. These are focused checks for this increment, not a rerun of the complete legacy suite.

Recovery contract records the API, format, ownership, failure policy, and next M5 sequence. Replication to a trusted successor, authority selection and fencing, surviving-client frontier reconciliation, and actual planned/abrupt takeover remain required. M4/M5 and the full-roadmap goal remain active.

Checkpoint replication increment#

replay/recovery now transfers bounded archive chunks to an explicitly trusted transport peer/binding. It repairs loss/reordering/duplication, rate-limits output, validates the whole archive and custom policy support, and acknowledges the exact SHA-256 archive identity. A new offer names the authority's last acknowledged archive to retain, so losing a newer Ready receipt cannot strand the authority with a reference to an evicted checkpoint. Failed/partial transfers preserve the stored archives. Receipt guarantees concern process memory, not disk durability.

Eight native tests and WASM instantiation pass. Cases include malformed offers and chunk indices, timeout/retry, wrong senders, same-archive binding replacement, lost Ready/canceled replacement, semantic archive rejection, unsupported custom room policy, and a private cave archive larger than the transport packet limit. The net suite's 24 native tests and WASM check also pass after tightening archive configuration validation against the restored runner's minimum egress requirement.

The real Godot ENet gate passes with 120 ms receive delay on each process, 20 ms jitter, 10% unreliable loss and 10% duplication:

Text
REPLAY_REPLICA_CAPTURE bytes=75591 tick=49 cpu_us=39591
REPLAY_REPLICA_SENDER_OK tick=49 elapsed_ms=2043 tx_bytes=173838 retries=95
REPLAY_REPLICA_SUCCESSOR_OK bytes=75591 tick=49 validation_us=193712 restore_us=108260
REPLAY_REPLICA_ENET_OK

The archive contains the real cave model after looting and throwing a rock, plus 72,000 bytes of authority-only fixture data. The successor validates, restores the complete frame under epoch 2, and advances simulation. The gate does not promote it into a network authority or migrate surviving players; it specifically proves the transfer/restore component. Both new gates are registered in tests/run_all.sh. The actual generated Godot probe also type-checks for WASM; no browser runtime is claimed. An initial Odin debug-build crash did not reproduce in subsequent direct and normal builds; no compiler fix is claimed.

These are single debug-run measurements, not performance percentiles. The observed encode/validation setup cost makes reusable canonical schema metadata a concrete follow-up before frequent large-world replication. Shared-wire dispatch, combined traffic scheduling, coordinator-approved fencing, and surviving-client recovery remain the next integration steps. Original frameworks and games remain untouched.

Gameplay integration and archive codec reuse#

Checkpoint_Codec now keeps canonical schema metadata across archive operations. The cached path produces identical bytes and retains content/type/value/contract validation; misuse with another type set is rejected. Receivers warm the codec during initialization, and the new replication link warms its publisher when a target is selected. The same 75,591-byte debug ENet fixture recorded:

Operation Earlier run Warm-metadata run
Capture/encode 39,591 us 1,574 us
Accumulated receiver processing/validation 193,712 us 7,304 us

These are individual instrumentation receipts, not a statistical benchmark. Fresh server restore still builds runtime schemas (139,521 us in the warm run).

transport.Router provides separate bounded packet/byte queues over one underlying connection and a combined output budget with gameplay capacity reserved. Reliable overflow retains the packet; unreliable background overflow can be repaired by the replication protocol. recovery.Link connects this router to the actual authority/ client runner, periodically captures checkpoints, preserves target sequence numbers across reauthorization, and stops sending/acknowledging work when that admitted connection is removed or changes generation. Backup failures do not stop gameplay.

The Godot Session now owns this integration. The application explicitly authorizes a recipient with session_backup_seat; receivers opt in. The Cavecrawl gate proved live movement, loot, and door actions while both endpoints agreed on checkpoint sequence 8 at tick 99 over the same ENet connection, with 120 ms receive delay each, 20 ms jitter, 10% loss and 10% duplication:

Text
REPLAY_CAVE_BACKUP_HOST tick=99 sequence=8
REPLAY_CAVE_BACKUP_CLIENT tick=99 sequence=8
REPLAY_CAVE_REPLICATION_OK

Focused validation passed: 25 runner tests, 9 recovery tests, 8 transport tests, WASM instantiation of the integrated link and generated cave scripts, the large ENet archive gate, live Cavecrawl replication, and both existing cave save/crash recovery gates. The native integration fixture also checks that an unselected observer receives no archive, game protocols reject no misrouted backup packets, same-peer retargeting progresses, and kicking the recipient stops backup work. The new live gate is registered in the main suite. The full legacy suite was not rerun for this additive increment.

Next: coordinator-approved leadership/fencing, partition behavior, and surviving- client frontier reconciliation, followed by actual planned and abrupt host takeover. The full M0–M9 goal remains active; original Kit/game/Scrapyard sources remain unchanged.

Authority decisions and lease enforcement#

replay/authority now implements one-room authority decisions over an explicit durable-CAS callback: trusted member/incarnation eligibility, bootstrap grants, deduplicated renewals, successor nomination, prepared checkpoint claims, planned retirement, abrupt expiry, coordinator restart quarantine, and epoch/revision floors. A failed commit or reversed clock fences the instance. The current test backend is an in-memory ledger, not a production durable service.

Correlated Lease replies derive a conservative local deadline from the request start, with bounded clock drift and margin. Native clocks include suspended time on macOS/Linux/Windows; unsupported targets fail closed. Mac runtime and Linux/ Windows/WASM type-checks pass. Prepared keeps an owned archive beyond receiver slot lifetime and only restores under the exact live owner grant.

The network runner checks required permits at input, packet, send, and simulation boundaries. A new timeline commit gate checks again after simulation but before publishing the candidate; the complete history ring and action frontier survive expiry during a tick. The client also restores its pending prediction flag. Godot Session exposes a fenced pause and clears fixed-step backlog.

Twelve authority tests pass, including opposite clock drift, delayed/replayed replies, storage failure and coordinator replacement, competing claims, consecutive migrations and old-host return, eligibility, canonical decision records, prepared archive lifetime/restore, and server/client expiry during simulation. Fourteen core, 25 runner, and 9 recovery tests also pass. The Godot native-clock gate ran the real cave model, stopped at tick 20 on lease expiry, and rejected a late renewal:

Text
REPLAY_LEASE_GODOT_OK stopped_tick=20 elapsed_ms=1184

The new gates are registered in the main suite. The existing live cave replication gate also passes after the protocol change. This increment changes experimental network protocol to 4 and archive format to 2, preserving require_permit across checkpoints; old Replay archives reject explicitly. Original Kit saves and games are untouched. Earlier performance/archive-size receipts describe their then-current formats.

The authority contract specifies assumptions and limits. It does not claim a deployed coordinator, production durability, Byzantine host resistance, resource-side effect fencing, or actual real-process host takeover. Next: authenticated coordinator RPCs and durable storage, then endpoint/epoch discovery, surviving-client frontier reconciliation, and planned/crash takeover acceptance. M5 and the full roadmap remain active.

The final Hello four-process protocol gate also passes. One cave recovery run failed its guest's post-resume inventory assertion; the instrumented rerun passed. Review identified an independent-shutdown race in that harness: the host could quit before a delayed/resyncing guest inspected its state, and unavailable probe state reads as zero. The host now waits for an explicit guest-verification marker, and the guest waits for state availability while retaining the same conservation checks. Normal recovery and a forced 1,800 ms guest stall both pass. This change does not disable cave combat or alter gameplay rules.

Authenticated coordinator service and SQLite decisions#

The authority package now exposes authenticated control RPCs and a client wrapper that correlates replies with its Lease. Per-participant HMAC-SHA-256 keys, process identity, client nonce, request sequence, and request hash bind the conversation. The service stages a command and commits its decision/result/replay frontier in a single durable CAS, including Query and rejected commands. Old mutations cannot follow a newer read or reexecute after restart; retrying a renewal does not extend the lease again. Decision record format is now version 2; the gameplay protocol and checkpoint format remain 4/2.

The native SQLite adapter verifies WAL/FULL synchronization, enables fullfsync, serializes CAS with BEGIN IMMEDIATE, and requires explicit file creation. The Nix toolchain now includes SQLite. Two store tests cover reopen/stale competing CAS and write failure; a subprocess killed mid-transaction recovers the previous epoch, known tick, and request frontier. This verifies process-crash recovery on this Mac, not physical power-loss behavior or arbitrary filesystem durability.

Nineteen authority tests and WASM instantiation pass. The service also passed a real three-process Godot gate with an actual cave checkpoint and private fixture data. The old owner retired, the successor restored at epoch 2, and the old process verified that it remained fenced. The coordinator was then killed and reopened from SQLite while the successor stayed alive. After quarantine, the successor resumed its retained world under epoch 3:

Text
REPLAY_SERVICE_READY generation=1 epoch=0
REPLAY_SERVICE_OLD_OWNER_FENCED
REPLAY_SERVICE_TRANSFER_READY epoch=2 tick=49
REPLAY_SERVICE_READY generation=2 epoch=2
REPLAY_SERVICE_RESTART_OK epoch=3 generation=2 tick=152
REPLAY_AUTHORITY_SERVICE_OK

The unchanged owner can now recover after a coordinator restart with either its retained current world or the exact checkpoint in a previously committed but unconsumed grant. A new epoch and quarantine are mandatory. Retired leases can receive control metadata without becoming valid gameplay permits again.

The service contract records APIs, trust, durability, and scope. The gate uses explicit fixture provisioning and a separate checkpoint connection; it does not yet migrate surviving game clients. Next: member/endpoint provisioning and the session driver for endpoint/epoch changes, pending-action reconciliation, and planned/crash takeover in the playable games. M5 and the full roadmap remain active. Original framework/game sources are intact.

Surviving-client migration and the Room driver#

net.client_authority now quarantines old pending actions until the new Welcome resolves the durable frontiers. Applied, rejected, retained, retired, and unknown settled outcomes are distinct. New sequence allocation starts from the recovered ledger, avoiding gaps after unreplicated work is lost. Old-host local pending actions are carried into rejoin reconciliation, and promoted clients obtain the same report against their prepared checkpoint. Recovery validates complete verdict frontiers before resetting prediction.

The presentation journal can end an epoch with explicit cancellations. Session preserves/drains those changes across role replacement, and Cavecrawl now keys verdict display by epoch plus sequence. A prior cancellation cannot masquerade as a new accepted action. The Room driver combines the authenticated control client, lease, gameplay Session, prepared copies, periodic replication, final freeze/release, takeover, old-host rejoin, and surviving-client redirect/retry. It reports actual checkpoint tick separately from the later Welcome tick, known rollback, and local protocol interruption. The cave HUD shows recovery and known rollback.

Four-process gates now keep a guest running through both planned handoff and a killed host. The guest retains its three gems and issues a freshly acknowledged door action in epoch 2. Planned mode also rejoins the old host as a player, and the service's reported recovery kind is checked. Example receipts:

Text
REPLAY_MIGRATION_GUEST_OK epoch=2 migrations=1 checkpoint=108 known_lost=0 interruption_ms=414
REPLAY_MIGRATION_PLANNED_OK
REPLAY_MIGRATION_GUEST_OK epoch=2 migrations=1 checkpoint=101 known_lost=7 interruption_ms=745
REPLAY_MIGRATION_CRASH_OK

Gameplay receive delay is 120 ms per process. An additional planned run passed with 20 ms jitter, 10% loss, and 10% duplication. These are single-run receipts, not percentile latency measurements. The latest native suites pass 29 runner, 12 presentation, and 20 authority cases, with WASM type-checks. Standalone cave play, save/resume and live replication also passed after the Session integration. An Odin WASM-check process exited unexpectedly once; the subsequent check passed without a source workaround, and no compiler fix is claimed.

The Room contract documents the new API and limits. This is substantial M5 progress, not its full completion: dynamic incarnation/ endpoint provisioning, successor loss, repeated and partitioned real migrations, return of a killed host, broader combat cases, and a competitive migration gate still need implementation/evidence. Original Kit and game projects remain separate.

Fresh process identities and extended live recovery#

Known members now obtain a service-assigned increasing incarnation through an authenticated, expiring Challenge/Rebind exchange. Challenges bind the client nonce, endpoint, current incarnation, and coordinator generation; they change no durable identity until a valid proof commits. Permissions and game-token binding remain provisioner-owned. Old proofs, old nonces, expired challenges, and proofs from a previous coordinator instance cannot reactivate a process. A currently leased authority cannot be replaced through registration.

The gameplay Hello/checkpoint now carries incarnation metadata. Room checks it against the authenticated roster and the stable game-token hash, resolves the successor's latest incarnation, and rejects stale-instance packets. A validated new instance reclaims its reserved seat and action frontier. The current experimental versions are gameplay protocol 5, checkpoint 3, control RPC 2, and decision record 3; old experimental formats require explicit conversion.

The live Cavecrawl matrix now additionally passes:

Text
REPLAY_MIGRATION_RETURNED_OK incarnation=103 seat=1
REPLAY_MIGRATION_RETURN_OK
REPLAY_MIGRATION_GUEST_OK epoch=3 migrations=2 checkpoint=142 known_lost=0 interruption_ms=919
REPLAY_MIGRATION_REPEAT_OK
REPLAY_MIGRATION_PARTITION_OK
REPLAY_MIGRATION_SUCCESSOR_LOSS_OK

The returned-host test kills the original process, completes migration, starts a fresh process, checks its newer incarnation/original seat, and performs a new accepted action. The repeated test keeps the guest alive through two handoffs. The partition test suppresses only the old host's control pumping, verifies a fixed game head after lease expiry, and rejoins it after the successor takes over. The loss test kills the selected successor during handoff and recovers the frozen surviving owner under a new epoch. If release already sealed a checkpoint, fallback requires that exact world hash/tick/size. Neither path revives a retired epoch or merges divergent inventories.

Focused checks pass: 30 network tests, 24 authority tests, 9 recovery tests, SQLite reopen/CAS/failure tests and its killed-writer recovery gate, the authenticated service handoff/restart gate, Hello network gameplay, and the generated cave's WASM type-check. New extended/partition gates are registered in the main test list. See registration for the precise guarantees.

M5 still needs fuller combat/loot timing coverage and competitive migration, along with broader deployment/provisioning UX. The next work can exercise these mechanisms in the competitive examples while continuing M4's remaining co-op primitives/parity. The full M0–M9 goal remains active. Original Kit, games, and Scrapyard remain intact.
